title: Cap. X Arg. III: even if Rom. ix is read only of temporal honor of Jacob over Esau, by theologians' consent Paul introduced it to represent eternal predestination/reprobation — not from contrary merits of works
pass_a_gloss: I know that some by no means grant that the aforesaid words of the Apostle are to be referred unto the everlasting predestination and reprobation of Jacob and Esau, but only unto that purpose whereby God of his good pleasure established to honor Jacob, and to subject Esau unto him, at least in the posterity of both. Be it so: Yet from the consent of Theologians, and from the whole discourse of the Apostle, that is clear, that this example was introduced by Paul at least unto representing the mystery of everlasting predestination and reprobation, and unto demonstrating by an argument from the figure unto the thing figured, that neither the election of men unto everlasting salvation, nor reprobation, is from contrary merits of works, but that God of the sole choice of his will elects some unto salvation, but reprobates others.
pass_b_english: I know some will not grant that those Apostolic words refer to Jacob and Esau's eternal predestination and reprobation — only to that purpose by which God of his good pleasure established to honor Jacob and subject Esau to him, at least in both their posterities. Be it so. Still, from theologians' consent and from the Apostle's whole discourse, this is clear: Paul introduced that example at least to represent the mystery of eternal predestination and reprobation, and to prove by argument from figure to thing figured that neither election of men to everlasting salvation, nor reprobation, is from contrary merits of works — but that God, of the sole choice of his will, elects some to salvation and reprobates others.
source_text: Scio nonnullos minime concedere praedicta Apostoli verba ad aeternam praedestinationem et reprobationem Jacobi et Esavi esse referenda, sed solummodo ad illud propositum quo constituit Deus pro beneplacito suo honorare Jacobum, et subjicere illi Esavum, saltem in posteris utriusque. Sit ita: Tamen ex consensu Theologorum, et ex toto discursu Apostoli illud liquet, hoc exemplum fuisse introductum a Paulo saltem ad repraesentandum aeternae praedestinationis et reprobationis mysterium, atque demonstrandum argumento a figura ad rem figuratam, neque electionem hominum ad aeternam salutem, neque reprobationem esse ex contrariis operum meritis, sed Deum ex solo voluntatis suae arbitrio alios eligere ad salutem, alios autem reprobare.
